newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea June note default ratio falls to 0.22 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea June note default ratio falls to 0.22 pct.

text.p: The ratio of South Korea's defaults on notes edged lower to 0.22 percent in June from 0.23 percent in May, the central Bank of Korea said on Tuesday.
But the June rate was still higher than 0.10 percent recorded in the same month a year ago, the bank said in a statement.
The notes would include such debts as promissory notes and bank cheques.
The bank said the ratio eased in June as note defaults declined by affiliate firms of financially troubled Hanbo Group, Sammi Group and Samlip General Foods Co.
Samlip, the nation's leading confectioner, had filed for court protection after defaulting on debt payments in May.
The nation's second-largest steelmaker Hanbo Steel Co collapsed in January, followed by specialty stainless steel products maker Sammi Steel Co in March.
The central bank said 1.67 trillion won worth of notes were not honoured in June out of a total 746.3 trillion won that should have been repaid.
The number of defaulting companies rose to 1,215 in June, against 758 a year ago and 1,257 in May, it said.
